--- title: "Speed up analysis with lazyframes in polars" subtitle: "scan_csv" author: '{{< var author >}}' date: '2025-09-22' date-format: iso toc: true toc-title: 'Sections' toc-location: right toc-depth: 3 categories: [100DaysOfPolars] --- Datasets are getting bigger, which means loading the entire dataset into memory can put a strain on your computer. Fortunately, Polars allows you to scan data and store it in a lazyframe before loading it into memory as a dataframe. Say we have this CSV file: ::: {#45eb63ab .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} csv_file = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jorammutenge/learn-rust/refs/heads/main/sample_sales.csv' ``` ::: ## Create a lazyframe by scanning a CSV file To read a CSV file as a lazyframe, you use the Polars expression `scan_csv`, like this: ::: {#973e20b9 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl (pl.scan_csv(csv_file) .select('Account Name','ext price') .group_by('Account Name') .agg(pl.mean('ext price')) .collect() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

Doing computations on a lazyframe is faster because nothing is stored in memory until you `collect` the results. Click to join 150+ students learning {{< var polars_course >}}.
